summary: Wooden tower of 1938 replaced by a 27.4 m steel tower about 1950 and moved six miles by helicopter in 1959; staffing listed to 2001; no source says if it still stands.

facts.design: Steel tower that replaced a wooden tower built in 1938
facts.status_note: No source confirms whether the steel tower still stands.
facts.agency: Saskatchewan forestry branch, fire control division (per the 1959 report)

events.note: Wooden fire tower built at the northern end of the trail to the Fishing Lakes.
A steel tower replaced the wooden one. The tour dates the change to about 1950; Canada Lookouts gives 1950.
Dismantled and moved six miles by helicopter to the Hanson Lake road, to be re-erected near the north end of Narrow Lake.
Towermen list gives Ralph Johnson at Narrow Hills among three towers, 1960 to 1987.
Towermen list gives Sheryl Fabish at Narrow Hills, 1997 to 2001.
Last year on the list for Narrow Hills. A note on the same list says the last tower was manned after mid-August 2001.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The tour account says the steel tower went up about 1950, and Canada Lookouts gives 1950. The two fit the same change, so the story says 'in about 1950'.

notes_for_editor: Brief status 'unknown' kept; no source says whether the steel tower stands today or whether the site is open. The tour account is undated and describes the tower on the road from Lower Fishing Lake with a museum in the original ranger's log cabin. It is not clear whether that is the 1959 site near Narrow Lake, so the story does not say so. The brief's agency (Saskatchewan Public Safety Agency) is not named in any source read here; the sources name the Department of Natural Resources and, in 1959, the forestry branch's fire control division. Check the current manager before relying on the agency field. The towermen-list note about all towers being condemned sits on the same list and names North Cabin, not Narrow Hills; the story reports it with that caveat.
